extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, patent agents, law schools (clinic administrators and faculty), and law students participating in USPTO clinic programs
extracted.subtask_short: USPTO practitioner conduct and clinic requirements
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory standards governing practitioner status (suspension, inactivation, resignation, revocation, reinstatement), reciprocal recognition for trademark practice, qualifications and obligations for law school clinic participation (faculty supervisors and students), reporting/inactivation/removal procedures for clinics, signature/certification requirements for filings, and disciplinary jurisdiction/grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response to notice to show cause (administrative suspension)
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner served with notice to show cause shall have 30 days from the date of the notice to file a response with the USPTO Director; the response should address any factual and legal bases why the practitioner should not be administratively suspended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The practitioner must serve a copy of the response on the OED Director at the time it is filed. The OED Director may file a reply within 10 days of receiving the copy. If the USPTO Director finds no genuine issues of material fact regarding the Office's compliance with notice requirements or the practitioner's failure to pay requisite fees, the USPTO Director shall enter an order administratively suspending the practitioner; otherwise the notice shall be dismissed. Requests for reconsideration of the USPTO Director's decision must be filed within 20 days after the decision; an administratively suspended practitioner may not obtain a stay of suspension during review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for administrative suspension (grounds considered)
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director will enter an administrative suspension if there are no genuine issues of material fact concerning the Office's compliance with notice requirements or the practitioner's failure to pay requisite fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determination is factual/legal; if genuine issues exist, suspension should be dismissed. The OED Director may withdraw the notice to show cause if the practitioner complies with the notice’s requirements prior to an order being entered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition during administrative suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: An administratively suspended practitioner is prohibited from practicing before the Office in patent matters while suspended and is subject to discipline for failing to comply with this prohibition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A practitioner who knows they have been administratively suspended and practices is subject to discipline and must comply with the provisions of § 11.116.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative reinstatement from suspension (general requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: An administratively suspended registered practitioner (or person with limited recognition) may be reinstated if they meet specific criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must not be the subject of a disciplinary investigation or party to a disciplinary proceeding; must apply on an OED form; demonstrate good moral character, reputation, and competence in advising/prosecuting patent applications; submit a declaration or affidavit attesting they have read the most recent revisions of patent laws and rules of practice; pay the fees set forth in § 1.21(a)(9)(ii) and all applicable delinquency fees in § 1.21(a)(9)(i).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement petition if >5 years after suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners applying for reinstatement more than five years after the effective date of administrative suspension must file a petition and provide objective evidence of continued legal qualifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In addition to the standard reinstatement requirements, the petition must demonstrate the practitioner continues to possess the necessary legal qualifications to render valuable service to patent applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative inactivation for Office employment
rubrics_metrics.description: Registered practitioners who become employed by the Office must withdraw from client matters and notify the OED Director on the first day of employment; their register entry is endorsed as administratively inactive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon separation from the Office, administratively inactive practitioners may request reactivation by complying with the reactivation requirements in paragraph (f)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative inactivation for judicial officers
rubrics_metrics.description: Registered practitioners who serve as judges, full-time court commissioners, U.S. bankruptcy judges, U.S. magistrate judges, or retired judges eligible for temporary assignment and not engaged in practice may request administrative inactive status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The OED Director will endorse the practitioner's name as administratively inactive upon acceptance. Following separation from the bench, the practitioner may request reactivation under paragraph (f)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of administrative inactivity on professional responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: An administratively inactive practitioner remains subject to the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct and to proceedings and sanctions under §§ 11.19–11.58 for conduct that violates the rules prior to or during inactivity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative inactivity does not remove jurisdiction for past or concurrent misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary inactivation procedure and effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Any registered practitioner may voluntarily enter inactive status by filing a written request; upon acceptance, OED endorses the name as voluntarily inactive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A voluntarily inactive practitioner is subject to investigation and discipline for conduct prior to/during/after inactivation; prohibited from practicing in patent cases while voluntarily inactive and must comply with § 11.116. Restoration to active status requires written request, completed registration application, information about moral character and reputation under § 11.7(a)(2)(i), a declaration/affidavit attesting to having read recent revisions of patent laws and rules, and payment of fees per § 1.21(a)(7)(iii) and (iv).

rubrics_metrics.name: Resignation restrictions and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner may request to resign by notifying the OED Director in writing unless the practitioner is under investigation, probable cause has been found by a Committee on Discipline panel, or is a respondent in certain pending disciplinary proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon acceptance, the practitioner is no longer eligible to practice before the Office in patent matters, must continue to file change of address for five years, their name is endorsed as resigned and published in the Official Gazette, and they must comply with § 11.116. They remain subject to investigation and discipline for conduct occurring prior to, during, or after resignation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative revocation (grounds)
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director may revoke an individual's registration or limited recognition if the registration was issued through mistake or inadvertence, or the application contains materially false information or omits material information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When grounds appear to exist, OED Director issues a notice to show cause (served per § 11.35) stating the grounds; OED files a copy with the USPTO Director. The individual has 30 days to respond to the USPTO Director and must serve OED. The OED Director may reply within 10 days. If the USPTO Director finds no genuine issues of material fact regarding notice compliance or grounds, the Director shall enter an order revoking registration/recognition; otherwise the notice is dismissed. Oral hearing is not granted unless ordered by the USPTO Director. Requests for reconsideration must be filed within 20 days; no stay of revocation is permitted during review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility to practice in trademark and non-patent matters (attorneys)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any individual who is an attorney as defined in § 11.1 may represent others before the Office in trademark and other non-patent matters without additional registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registration as a patent practitioner does not itself entitle an individual to practice before the Office in trademark matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-lawyers and pre-1957 trademark agents
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals who are not attorneys are not recognized to practice in trademark matters, except those non-attorneys who were recognized to practice before January 1, 1957, will be recognized as agents to continue practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Except as provided, registration as a patent agent does not entitle trademark practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal recognition for foreign trademark practitioners (eligibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: A foreign attorney or agent (non-resident of U.S.) may be recognized for limited purpose of representing parties located in their country before the USPTO in trademark matters if they apply for reciprocal recognition and prove they are a registered and active member in good standing with their country's trademark office and possess good moral character and reputation, and there is an official understanding allowing substantially reciprocal privileges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognition continues only while these conditions are met. In any trademark matter where such a foreign practitioner represents an applicant/registrant/party, a U.S. attorney (per § 11.1) must also be appointed pursuant to § 2.17(b) and (c) as the representative who will file and correspond with the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application and fee for reciprocal recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: An individual seeking reciprocal recognition must apply in writing to the OED Director and pay the application fee required by § 1.21(a)(1)(i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Application must include evidence satisfying eligibility provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to provide and update contact information (reciprocal practitioners)
rubrics_metrics.description: A reciprocally recognized practitioner must provide the OED Director their postal address, at least one and up to three email addresses, and a business telephone number, and must provide changes to such information within 30 days of the change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to provide or timely update information may result in withdrawal of reciprocal recognition under paragraph (i). A reciprocally recognized practitioner must also notify the OED Director of any lapse in their authorization to represent clients before their country's trademark office within 30 days of the lapse.

rubrics_metrics.name: OED Director communications and proof of good standing (reciprocal practitioners)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director may send a letter to ascertain contact information and good standing; the recipient must provide contact information and, if requested, a certificate of good standing from their country's trademark office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to reply and provide requested information within a specified time limit may lead to withdrawal of reciprocal recognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal and reinstatement of reciprocal recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: Reciprocal recognition may be withdrawn if the practitioner is no longer registered/eligible in the foreign trademark office, no longer resides in the country on which recognition is based, or fails to provide required information; withdrawn practitioners may reapply for recognition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Withdrawal is prompt upon notice absent a showing of cause why recognition should not be withdrawn; reapplication follows the normal application process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility criteria for Law School Clinic Certification Program admission
rubrics_metrics.description: All ABA-accredited law schools are eligible to apply for participation; non-participating schools seeking admission and participating schools seeking to add practice areas must submit applications per OED criteria; renewals are biennial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The OED Director may refuse admission or renewal if participation would fail to provide significant benefit to the public or to the law students. Time periods and additional criteria are set by the OED Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement that clinic services be pro bono
rubrics_metrics.description: Each law school participating in the USPTO Law School Clinic Certification Program must provide its patent and/or trademark services on a pro bono basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program participation is contingent on pro bono provision in the relevant practice areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Faculty Clinic Supervisor qualifications — patent practice
rubrics_metrics.description: A Faculty Clinic Supervisor for patent practice must be a registered patent practitioner in active status and good standing and meet experience and supervisory requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically: be registered under § 11.6(a) or (b) and in active good standing with OED; demonstrate at least 3 years' experience prosecuting patent applications before the Office within the 5 years immediately prior to request; assume full responsibility for instruction and guidance of students; assume full responsibility for all patent applications and legal services (including filings) produced by the clinic; and comply with additional criteria established by the OED Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Faculty Clinic Supervisor qualifications — trademark practice
rubrics_metrics.description: A Faculty Clinic Supervisor for trademark practice must be an attorney and meet experience and supervisory requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically: be an attorney under § 11.1; demonstrate at least 3 years' experience prosecuting trademark applications before the Office within the 5 years immediately prior to request; assume full responsibility for instruction, guidance, and supervision of students; assume full responsibility for all trademark applications and legal services (including filings) produced by the clinic; and comply with additional criteria established by the OED Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Faculty Clinic Supervisor written statement of responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: A Faculty Clinic Supervisor must submit a statement assuming specific supervisory and administrative responsibilities for the clinic practice area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statement must: assume responsibility for performing conflicts checks for each student and client; assume responsibility for student instruction, mentoring, overseeing and supervising participating students; assume responsibility for content and timeliness of all applications and documents submitted to the Office; assume responsibility for all communications by clinic students to clinic clients; assume responsibility for ensuring no gap in representation during student turnover or schedule transitions; attest to meeting the applicable criteria in paragraph (c)(1) or (c)(2); and attest to other criteria established by the OED Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited recognition for law students — patent practice criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Law students may be granted limited recognition to practice in patent matters under the Clinic Program if they meet OED criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirements include: enrollment at an active participating law school; enrollment in the patent practice area of the clinic; successful completion of at least one year of law school (or equivalent); having read the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct and relevant patent practice rules; supervision by an approved Faculty Clinic Supervisor pursuant to paragraph (c)(1); and meeting any additional criteria established by the OED Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited recognition for law students — trademark practice criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Law students may be granted limited recognition to practice in trademark matters under the Clinic Program if they meet OED criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirements include: enrollment at an active participating law school; enrollment in the trademark practice area of the clinic; successful completion of at least one year of law school (or equivalent); having read the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct and relevant trademark practice rules; supervision by an approved Faculty Clinic Supervisor pursuant to paragraph (c)(2); certification by the dean (or authorized designee) that the student completed first year or equivalent, is in compliance with the law school's ethics code, and is of good moral character and reputation; the student must neither ask for nor receive any fee or compensation from clinic clients; and must comply with additional criteria established by the OED Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participation of already-registered students
rubrics_metrics.description: Students already registered to practice before the Office as patent agents or authorized to practice in trademark matters must still complete the student application and meet the clinic criteria to participate in the program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They must submit a student application per paragraph (d)(1) and meet the criteria in paragraphs (d)(2) or (d)(3) as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinic reporting requirements (semiannual)
rubrics_metrics.description: Participating law schools must provide OED with a semiannual report regarding clinic activity containing specified data elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report must include: number of law students participating in each practice area; number of faculty participating in each practice area; number of persons assisted without formation of practitioner-client relationship; number of client representations undertaken for each practice area; identity and number of applications and responses filed in each practice area; number of patents issued or trademarks registered to clinic clients; and any other information specified by the OED Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inactivation of law school clinic practice area (grounds and effects)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director may inactivate a patent and/or trademark practice area of a participating law school if the school lacks an approved Faculty Clinic Supervisor or fails to meet program requirements or for other good cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon inactivation, participating law school students must immediately cease all student practice before the Office in the relevant practice area, notify each client, and disassociate themselves from all client matters relating to practice before the Office, including complying with Office and State withdrawal rules. A practice area inactivated may be restored to active status upon application and approval by the OED Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Removal of law school clinic practice area (grounds and consequences)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director may remove a practice area from participation upon request of the law school, failure to meet program requirements, or other good cause; removal requires students to cease practice and disassociate as with inactivation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A school removed from participation may reapply in compliance with § 11.16.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature requirement for documents filed in the Office
rubrics_metrics.description: All documents filed in the Office in patent, trademark, and other non-patent matters (except correspondence required to be signed by applicant/party) must bear a signature personally signed or inserted by the practitioner, in compliance with § 1.4(d) or § 2.193(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The signature requirement applies to all filings and filings with hearing officers in disciplinary proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification obligations and sanctions for filings (statement of truth and inquiry)
rubrics_metrics.description: By presenting a paper to the Office or a hearing officer, the presenting party certifies that statements of their own knowledge are true, statements on information and belief are believed to be true, and that false statements may expose the presenter to penalties under 18 U.S.C. 1001 and other criminal statutes; and that, to the best of the signer's knowledge, information and belief formed after a reasonable inquiry, the paper is not presented for an improper purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The certification also requires that legal contentions are warranted by existing law or by a nonfrivolous argument for change, factual allegations have evidentiary support or are likely to after investigation, and denials of factual contentions are warranted on the evidence or reasonably based on lack of information. Violations of these certification obligations, after notice and opportunity to respond, may result in sanctions including striking the paper, referral to OED Director for action, preclusion from submitting papers or presenting/contesting issues, affecting the weight given to the paper, or terminating the proceedings. Practitioners may also be subject to disciplinary action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disciplinary jurisdiction (who is subject)
rubrics_metrics.description: All practitioners engaged in practice before the Office (including those administratively suspended, registered or recognized to practice, resigned or inactivated under § 11.11, authorized under § 41.5(a) or 42.10(c), transferred to disability inactive status or publicly disciplined by a duly constituted authority) are subject to the disciplinary jurisdiction of the Office. Non-practitioners who engage in or offer to engage in practice without authority are also subject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office's disciplinary jurisdiction is broad and includes practitioners regardless of administrative status when relevant to conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Grounds for discipline include conviction of a serious crime; discipline on ethical or professional misconduct grounds imposed in another jurisdiction or disciplinary disqualification from participating in or appearing before any Federal program or agency; failure to comply with any court order disciplining a practitioner or any final USPTO Director disciplinary decision; and violation of any USPTO Rule of Professional Conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These grounds apply whether the conduct was individual or in concert with others and whether or not done in the course of providing legal services or in a matter pending before the Office.
